problem_motivation.content: Porous triboelectric materials are promising but are hindered in practice by instability and humidity sensitivity.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Porous triboelectric materials offer significant potential for enhancing the performance of triboelectric nanogenerators, yet their practical application is limited by structural instability and humidity-induced performance degradation.

problem_motivation.content: TENG deployment is limited by instability in humid and repeated-loading conditions, motivating new materials strategies.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Despite these merits, their practical deployment is constrained by performance instability under realistic operating conditions, particularly in humid environments and under repeated (high cycle) mechanical loading [2,3].

problem_motivation.content: There is a need for designs that preserve both mechanical integrity and environmental robustness.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: These limitations underscore the need for material design strategies that will simultaneously ensure a long-term mechanical integrity and environmental robustness.

prior_approach.content: Prior work added FEP powder into porous PDMS sponge to boost output.
prior_approach.evidence_span: For instance, Kou et al. incorporated fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP) powder into a porous polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) sponge and achieved 1.2 times higher output than the pristine porous film [7].

prior_approach.content: Prior work infiltrated carbon nanotubes into porous PDMS to make a humidity sensor.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Vafaiee et al. fabricated a humidity sensor by infiltrating carbon nanotubes into a porous PDMS matrix

prior_approach.content: Existing porosity-generation methods include template-assisted processing, emulsion, phase separation, gas foaming, solid-state sintering, and 3D printing.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Common ways to introduce porosity include template-assisted approach [5,9,10], emulsion [11,12], phase separation [13,14], gas foaming [15], solid-state sintering [16] and 3D printing [17].

prior_approach.content: MOFs such as hydrophilic HKUST-1 have been widely used for humidity sensing.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), such as the hydrophilic HKUST-1, possess well-defined microporous structures and strong affinity toward water molecules [23]. While they are widely explored for humidity sensing

prior_approach.content: HKUST-1 synthesis followed a previously reported procedure with slight modifications.
prior_approach.evidence_span: HKUST-1 crystals were synthesized following a previously reported procedure with slight modifications [27].

prior_limitation.content: These foaming methods are time-consuming or restricted to certain polymers.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, these foaming approaches are either time-consuming or limited to specific classes of polymers.

rejected_alternative.content: External templating is avoided because the material intrinsically self-foams.
A 2D representative area element was used instead of a more expensive model to reduce computational cost while retaining key behavior.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: To reduce computational cost while retaining the essential deformation and charge transfer characteristics, a two-dimensional (2D) representative area element (RAE) was employed under quasi-static loading conditions.

rejected_alternative.content: Foaming used a solvent-assisted route instead of chemical blowing or templating agents.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: the foaming process was achieved purely on a solvent-assisted approach, without the use of additional chemical blowing/templating agents

inspiration_source.content: Interpretation of porous mechanical response draws on the Gibson–Ashby cellular solids model.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: Such behaviour is consistent with the classical deformation model of cellular solids described by Gibson and Ashby [33].

causal_claim.content: Adding HKUST-1 fillers reinforces the membrane and regulates moisture effects.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Hydrophilic MOF fillers comprising HKUST-1 crystals are incorporated within the porous matrix to reinforce the membrane structure and regulate moisture effects.

causal_claim.content: HKUST-1 reduces humidity-driven charge loss by trapping water in its framework, improving output stability at higher humidity.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In addition, HKUST-1 mitigates humidity-induced charge dissipation by confining water molecules within its framework, giving enhanced triboelectric output stability and reduced performance degradation under increasing relative humidity compared to the neat porous system.

causal_claim.content: Porosity lowers effective modulus and stiffness, enabling greater deformation and contact compliance.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The introduction of porosity reduces the effective modulus and hence mechanical stiffness of the material, enabling larger deformation under applied stress for enhanced contact compliance, particularly under low-force stimuli [4].

causal_claim.content: This mechanical adaptability improves charge generation relative to dense materials.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This mechanical adaptability facilitates improved charge generation compared to dense counterparts.

causal_claim.content: Porous architecture improves breathability and stretchability, increasing comfort in wearables.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The porous architecture also improves breathability and stretchability of the material, thereby enhancing comfort when deployed in wearable devices [5].

causal_claim.content: Internal voids enable incorporation of functional fillers for higher output or added functionality.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Moreover, the presence of internal voids offers a versatile platform for incorporating functional fillers, enabling an even higher output or additional functionalities within the triboelectric system [6].

causal_claim.content: Air as a secondary phase lowers dielectric constant and limits charge storage.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In addition, the inclusion of air as a secondary phase lowers the effective dielectric constant, limiting charge storage capability [20].

causal_claim.content: Porous architectures have lower mechanical robustness and are prone to pore collapse and densification under high stress.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Mechanically, porous architectures inherently suffer from reduced mechanical robustness, making them susceptible to pore collapse and structural densification under high stress, especially when smaller pore sizes are involved [21].

causal_claim.content: Interconnected pores allow moisture ingress, forming adsorbed water layers that promote charge leakage and degrade TENG performance in humidity.
causal_claim.evidence_span: More critically, the interconnected pore network facilitates moisture ingress, leading to the formation of adsorbed water layers that promote charge leakage, which will significantly degrade the electrical performance of TENG devices under humid conditions [22].

causal_claim.content: Confining water and enhancing dielectric properties can mitigate charge screening and humidity-induced degradation while preserving compliance.
causal_claim.evidence_span: By temporary confinement of water molecules and enhancement of the dielectric properties, such hydrophilic fillers can mitigate charge screening and protect against humidity-induced performance degradation, while preserving the intrinsic mechanical compliance of porous structures [25].

causal_claim.content: Disulfide linkages enable self-foaming to create porous architectures without external templating.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The introduction of disulfide bonds also enables a self-foaming process to generate porous architectures without any external templating.

causal_claim.content: Intrinsic foaming simplifies fabrication and offers an environmentally benign route to porous materials.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This intrinsic foaming capability not only simplifies film fabrication but also offers a facile route towards environmentally benign porous materials.

causal_claim.content: Embedded HKUST-1 reinforces structure and stabilizes electrical output under load and humidity.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The resulting porous structure provides a framework for embedding HKUST-1 fillers, which act to reinforce structural integrity and stabilize electrical output under mechanical loading and humid conditions.

causal_claim.content: Ambient moisture uptake by NMP triggers solvent–non-solvent exchange and phase separation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Upon exposure of the heated, concentrated polymer solution to ambient moisture, the hygroscopic NMP solvent absorbs water and initiates a solvent-non-solvent exchange, leading to phase separation into a polymer-rich phase and a solvent-rich phase.

causal_claim.content: Solidification of the polymer-rich phase and evaporation of the solvent-rich phase produce pores.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The polymer-rich phase undergoes solidification, facilitated by the annealing process of the disulfide bonds. Meanwhile the solvent-rich phase evaporates, creating voids within the polymer matrix and resulting in a porous structure

causal_claim.content: Changing polymer concentration tunes pore size, which first rises then falls.
causal_claim.evidence_span: With increasing solution concentration, the pore size initially increases and then decreases.

causal_claim.content: Too-low concentration gives poor viscosity and nonuniform foaming.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Although lower concentrations promote larger pore formation, excessively low concentrations lead to poor viscosity, resulting in non-uniform surface foaming.

causal_claim.content: Low humidity prevents foaming because exchange is insufficient.
causal_claim.evidence_span: foaming does not occur under low-humidity conditions due to an insufficient solvent-non-solvent exchange rate

causal_claim.content: Excess humidity destabilizes pores by trapping residual solvent.
causal_claim.evidence_span: an excessively high humidity also hinders phase separation, as the solvent-rich phase evaporates less efficiently, leading to residual solvent entrapment within the pores, which makes the porous architecture less stable

causal_claim.content: Low temperature prevents stable porous-network formation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: At lower temperatures, the slow solvent-non-solvent exchange prevents the formation of a stable porous network

causal_claim.content: High temperature yields dense nonporous film via enhanced polymer solubility.
causal_claim.evidence_span: at higher temperatures, enhanced polymer solubility results in a dense, non-porous film

causal_claim.content: Charging speed decreases as capacitor capacitance increases.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Figure 3f demonstrates that the energy harvested from the TENG device can be used to charge capacitors, where the charging speed went down as the capacitance increased.

causal_claim.content: Repeated loading increases output voltage.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Notably, the output voltage gradually increases with repeated loading cycles.

causal_claim.content: Framework reinforcement stabilizes the porous structure and makes compression response more elastic and less dissipative.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As a result, the porous structure is stabilized, and the mechanical response transitions toward a more elastic and less dissipative behavior under compression.

causal_claim.content: When local stress reaches yield, cell walls buckle or collapse, causing nonlinear stress-strain behavior.
causal_claim.evidence_span: When this stress reaches the yield point, until the polymer can no longer sustain elasticity at a higher stress level, the cell walls will buckle or even collapse and leads to non-linearity in the stress-strain curve.

causal_claim.content: Low stiffness at low stress allows efficient deformation and near-linear output increase.
causal_claim.evidence_span: under low stress level, the output increases almost linearly with increasing stress, as the relatively low stiffness of the porous structure allows efficient deformation under small loads

causal_claim.content: Post-yield changes in thickness and area make capacitance and potential output nonlinear.
causal_claim.evidence_span: After the material reaches its initial yield stress, the concurrent change in thickness and surface area leads to nonlinear change in the capacitance level, which gives nonlinear response in the potential output at the same time.

causal_claim.content: Strain hardening alone causes a plateau, not the high-stress voltage jump.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the non-linear behavior alone, in particular the strain-hardening response, does not lead to the jump in voltage at higher stress levels, but rather a plateau behavior

causal_claim.content: Pore closure creates additional contact interfaces, increasing surface charge and electrode potential difference.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This additional contact interfaces induced by pore closure creates additional surface charge and larger potential difference between the back electrodes

causal_claim.content: In the linear elastic regime, proportional contact-area growth with stress gives linear electrical output.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As the contact area between the triboelectric layers increases almost proportionally with the applied stress, the electrical output also exhibits a linear response.

causal_claim.content: Progressive strain hardening lowers stress sensitivity and creates a voltage plateau.
causal_claim.evidence_span: progressive strain hardening increases the effective stiffness of the porous framework, requiring higher stresses to yield additional deformation. Consequently, the stress sensitivity gradually decreases, giving rise to a nearly plateau region observed in the voltage response.

causal_claim.content: Widespread pore collapse in densification sharply increases contact area and voltage.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Upon reaching the densification regime, widespread pore collapse leads to a sharp increase in contact area, which results in the observed abrupt increase in voltage.

causal_claim.content: HKUST-1 filler support resists pore collapse and eliminates the sudden voltage jump.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the HKUST-1 reinforced structure resists pore collapses due to the mechanical support provided by the fillers, thereby suppressing this instability and eliminating the sudden voltage jump

causal_claim.content: Greater hydrophobicity should improve resistance to humidity.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the HKUST-1-loaded porous film appears to be the most hydrophobic film and thus leads to better resistance to increased humidity

causal_claim.content: This adsorption lowers air fraction in pores and raises local dielectric constant.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Such adsorption effectively reduces the air fraction inside the pores and increases the local dielectric constant.

causal_claim.content: Higher effective permittivity enhances charge retention and causes the observed voltage increase.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The presence of these dielectric inclusions enhances the overall effective permittivity of the composite membrane and promotes surface charge retention, leading to the observed voltage increase

causal_claim.content: Adsorbed water films increase ionic mobility and create percolative conduction pathways that accelerate charge loss.
causal_claim.evidence_span: These adsorbed water films increase ionic mobility and facilitate the formation of percolative conduction pathways, which accelerate charge dissipation and recombination.

causal_claim.content: This effect reduces output in dense and porous films.
causal_claim.evidence_span: For both the dense and the porous films, such effect leads to a decline in electrical output.

causal_claim.content: Continued water uptake by HKUST-1 partly offsets humidity damage via dielectric enhancement, maintaining high output up to 40% RH.
causal_claim.evidence_span: for the HKUST-1 loaded porous membrane, the high output is sustained, as continued water uptake by HKUST-1 partially offsets this effect by contributing to dielectric enhancement, facilitating the framework to maintain a relatively high output up to 40% RH, where the average open-circuit voltage diminished by only 4%.

causal_claim.content: Once HKUST-1 cavities saturate with water at high humidity, charge-retention benefit is lost and conductive pore filling dominates, sharply reducing output.
causal_claim.evidence_span: At even higher humidity levels, once the internal cavities of HKUST-1 become saturated with water, the MOF no longer effectively contributes to charge retention. The conductive pore-filling effect then dominates, resulting in a pronounced decline in output performance.

causal_claim.content: Dielectric enhancement from water-confined HKUST-1 and greater hydrophobicity help the composite retain higher output than controls.
causal_claim.evidence_span: due to dielectric enhancement of the water-confined HKUST-1 fillers and the higher hydrophobicity of the porous membrane, the HKUST-1 loaded porous membrane maintains a relatively higher output compared to the porous and the dense films

causal_claim.content: HKUST-1 incorporation enhances structural integrity, mitigating pore collapse and improving robustness under repeated loading.
causal_claim.evidence_span: By incorporating HKUST-1 within the porous matrix, the structural integrity of the system is effectively enhanced, mitigating pore collapse and improving mechanical robustness under repeated loading.

causal_claim.content: Maintaining pore stability is essential for consistent triboelectric performance.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The correlation between stress strain response and electrical output demonstrates that maintaining pore stability is essential for achieving consistent triboelectric performance.

causal_claim.content: Water confinement in HKUST-1 suppresses continuous conductive pathways and reduces humid charge dissipation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The confinement of water within the MOF structure suppresses the formation of continuous conductive pathways within the porous network, thereby reducing charge dissipation under humid conditions.

causal_claim.content: As a result, the composite membrane shows better humidity tolerance and more stable output than pristine porous material, especially at intermediate RH.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As a result, the composite membrane exhibits improved humidity tolerance and more stable electrical output compared to the pristine porous system, particularly at intermediate relative humidity levels.

mechanism_principle.content: Stable triboelectric output depends critically on maintaining pore stability.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: analysis of stress-strain behaviour reveals the critical role of pore stability in achieving stable triboelectric output

mechanism_principle.content: The reason HKUST-1 reduces humidity-induced charge dissipation is that it confines water molecules within its framework.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: HKUST-1 mitigates humidity-induced charge dissipation by confining water molecules within its framework

mechanism_principle.content: Moisture adsorption causes charge screening and dissipation, while cyclic deformation causes structural degradation and poor reliability.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Moisture adsorption on triboelectric surfaces can induce charge screening and accelerate charge dissipation, while structural degradation under cyclic deformation compromises long-term reliability.

mechanism_principle.content: Nylon's intramolecular hydrogen bonding and semicrystallinity make controlled pore formation difficult.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: its intramolecular hydrogen bonding and semicrystalline structure result in a narrow processing window, which makes controlled pore formation extremely difficult [18,19].

mechanism_principle.content: The proposed mitigation comes from temporary water confinement and enhanced dielectric properties of the filler.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: By temporary confinement of water molecules and enhancement of the dielectric properties

mechanism_principle.content: Differential pressure upon vacuum release drives HKUST-1 infiltration into membrane pores.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Upon gradual release of the vacuum, the differential pressure facilitated the infiltration of HKUST-1 crystals into the pores of the membrane.

mechanism_principle.content: Asymmetric vapor exposure causes a pore-size gradient because vapor diffuses more slowly toward the bottom.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The asymmetric exposure to ambient vapor during formation induces a pore size gradient across the membrane thickness, with larger pores predominantly formed near the surface, and progressively smaller ones towards the bottom due to slower vapor diffusion rate

mechanism_principle.content: Higher viscosity shrinks pore size because exchange slows and bubbles are retained.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The decreasing pore size at higher viscosity can be attributed to the slower solvent–non-solvent exchange rate and higher bubble retention.

mechanism_principle.content: Minimal interaction is consistent with physical infiltration rather than chemical bonding.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This result is consistent with the route by which the MOF crystals were physically infiltrated into the porous PA matrix.

mechanism_principle.content: Large pores reduce dielectric constant, contact area, and breakdown strength, causing lower output and leakage.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The reduced output is attributed to the large pore size, which lowers the effective dielectric constant of the material and decreases the effective contact area during operation. The void space within the porous framework also lowers the air breakdown voltage within the material, leading to easier charge leakage

mechanism_principle.content: HKUST-1 acts as dielectric inclusions and exposed particles increase interfacial contact, improving charge transfer.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The HKUST-1 crystals act as dielectric inclusions within the pores, partially restoring the effective dielectric constant of the composite membrane. In addition, the exposed MOF particles increase the effective interfacial contact area and promote charge transfer at the triboelectric interface.

mechanism_principle.content: Creep-induced thickness reduction strengthens the electric field and improves long-term output.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This enhancement can be attributed to a creep-induced thickness reduction of the foam under prolonged cyclic compression, which enhances the electric field strength, thereby improving its long-term output performance.

mechanism_principle.content: Initial indentation response comes from elastic bending of cell walls.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In the initial regime, the response is dominated by elastic bending of the cell walls, resulting in an approximately linear increase in load.

mechanism_principle.content: Plateau regime arises from elastic buckling of cell walls.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is followed by a plateau region associated with elastic buckling of the cell walls, which gives rise to reduced stiffness.

mechanism_principle.content: High-depth stiffening indicates pore collapse and densification.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: At higher indentation depths, a sharp increase in stiffness is observed as the pores collapse and the material densifies, indicating the transition to compression of the solid framework.

mechanism_principle.content: MOF fillers reinforce the framework, suppress buckling, and delay pore collapse.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This suggests that the MOF fillers act as mechanical reinforcements within the porous framework, suppressing cell wall buckling and delaying pore collapse.

mechanism_principle.content: Compression concentrates stress in vertically oriented cell walls, deforming pores elliptically and intensifying local stress.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Under compressive loading, the cell walls oriented perpendicular to the applied stress experience concentrated stress, leading to deformation of the pore into an elliptical shape with localized stress intensification.

mechanism_principle.content: The plateau comes from reduced incremental deformation at higher stiffness, limiting capacitance variation.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This behavior arises from the reduced incremental deformation at higher stiffness, where increasingly larger stresses are required to induce further structural changes, thereby limiting the variation in capacitance.

mechanism_principle.content: At low humidity, water coordinates to Cu2+ sites and is confined in HKUST-1 cavities.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: At low humidity, isolated water molecules coordinate with the Cu2+ paddlewheel sites and are temporarily confined within the internal cavities.

mechanism_principle.content: At 20–40% RH, capillary condensation forms thin water films on exposed surfaces.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: When the humidity exceeds 20% RH but below 40% RH, progressive water condensation within the confined pore space occurs due to capillary effects, leading to the formation of thin water layers along the exposed surface.

hypothesis_statement.content: The work proposes an integrated strategy combining self-foamed porosity, sustainable polymer design, and functional filler reinforcement to produce robust and environmentally stable triboelectric systems.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: This work demonstrates a strategy that integrates self-foamed porous structures, sustainable polymer design, and functional filler reinforcement to engineer mechanically robust and environmentally stable triboelectric systems.

hypothesis_statement.content: Adding functional fillers to porous matrices can reinforce mechanics and regulate environmental effects simultaneously.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To address the aforementioned challenges, incorporating functional fillers into porous matrices provides a viable pathway to simultaneously reinforce mechanical stability and regulate environmental effects.

hypothesis_statement.content: HKUST-1 can act as a moisture regulator in triboelectric systems by confining water in nanoscale cavities.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: their ability to confine and localize water molecules within internal nanosized cavities presents an alternative function as moisture regulators in triboelectric systems.

hypothesis_statement.content: The study reports an HKUST-1 integrated porous nylon-like membrane for improved robustness and humidity tolerance in TENGs.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Herein, we report a HKUST-1 integrated porous nylon-like membrane that achieves enhanced mechanical robustness and improved humidity tolerance for TENG applications.

hypothesis_statement.content: The work presents a composite design strategy to resolve the trade-off between compliance and environmental stability.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: and presents a composite material design strategy that addresses the inherent trade-off between mechanical compliance and environmental stability.

hypothesis_statement.content: The model assumes constant surface charge density while electrical output changes through expanded contact area under compression.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To investigate the influence of mechanical nonlinearity on electrical output, the surface charge density was assumed to remain constant throughout the simulation, while charge generation was allowed to occur in response to expanded contact area under compressive loading.

hypothesis_statement.content: Mechanical behavior and triboelectric output are strongly coupled.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The similarity between the mechanical response of the porous structure and its triboelectric output suggests a strong coupling between mechanical behavior and electrical performance.

hypothesis_statement.content: The simulated TENG output should scale approximately inversely with sample stiffness.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: It is shown that the simulated output of the TENG device scales almost inversely proportional to the stiffness of the sample.

hypothesis_statement.content: The voltage jump is attributed to pore-closure events exposing pore valleys under extreme compression.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Therefore, for a porous substrate, we ascribe the voltage jump to pore closure event instead, particularly due to the exposure of the pore valleys under extreme compression.

hypothesis_statement.content: The abrupt TENG output increase comes from pore-collapse geometric instability, not intrinsic material nonlinearity.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: the abrupt increase in TENG output originates not from intrinsic material nonlinearity, but from geometric instability associated with pore collapse

hypothesis_statement.content: Further optimization could come from adjusting HKUST-1 loading to balance compliance and moisture regulation.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Further optimization can be achieved by tailoring the loading fraction of HKUST-1 to balance mechanical compliance and moisture regulation.

hypothesis_statement.content: Tuning pore size and filler dimensions could extend performance under more extreme humidity.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: tuning the pore size and filler dimensions presents an effective route to extend device performance under more extreme humidity conditions.

hypothesis_statement.content: The porous platform could integrate other functional fillers for multifunctional self-powered devices.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The versatility of this porous platform also enables the integration of additional functional fillers, opening opportunities for multifunctional devices.

evidence_result.content: Mechanical tests show HKUST-1 prevents pore collapse and improves robustness during repeated deformation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Mechanical characterization demonstrates that HKUST-1 suppresses pore collapse and improves structural robustness under repeated deformation

evidence_result.content: The composite shows more stable triboelectric output and less degradation as relative humidity increases than the neat porous material.
evidence_result.evidence_span: giving enhanced triboelectric output stability and reduced performance degradation under increasing relative humidity compared to the neat porous system

evidence_result.content: FEP-filled porous PDMS gave 1.2× higher output than pristine porous film.
evidence_result.evidence_span: achieved 1.2 times higher output than the pristine porous film [7].

evidence_result.content: CNT infiltration increased humidity sensing response by 52% with linear behavior up to 80% RH.
evidence_result.evidence_span: which resulted in a 52% enhancement in humidity sensing response with a linear sensing behaviour of up to 80% relative humidity (RH) [8].

evidence_result.content: Water adsorption raises the dielectric constant of HKUST-1 by nearly twentyfold.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Water adsorption increases the dielectric constant of HKUST-1 crystals by nearly 20 times [24].

evidence_result.content: The study establishes a direct correlation between mechanical properties and triboelectric performance in a porous system.
evidence_result.evidence_span: This study establishes a direct correlation between mechanical properties and triboelectric performance in a porous system

evidence_result.content: 0.33 g mL−1 gave uniform foaming with relatively large pores.
evidence_result.evidence_span: 0.33 g mL-1 solution was used for subsequent studies because it produces uniform foaming while retaining a relatively large pore size of 16.8 ± 4.2 µm

evidence_result.content: Optimal foaming occurred near 20 °C and 40% RH.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We established that optimal foaming was achieved at approximately 20 °C and 40% RH, where a well-defined porous structure was obtained.

evidence_result.content: XRD confirms successful HKUST-1 crystal formation with the desired morphology and size.
evidence_result.evidence_span: These results confirm the successful formation of HKUST-1 crystals with desired morphology and size.

evidence_result.content: No significant FTIR difference between porous and dense membranes indicates no chemical reaction during foaming.
evidence_result.evidence_span: for the porous and dense membrane, no significant spectral difference was observed, which indicates that there is no chemical reaction during the foaming process, and the chemical structure of the polymer remains intact in the porous state

evidence_result.content: EDS copper signal confirms successful HKUST-1 infiltration.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the copper atom confirms the successful infiltration of the HKUST-1 MOF crystals

evidence_result.content: Raman mapping shows a sharp polymer–crystal boundary, implying minimal chemical interaction.
evidence_result.evidence_span: there is a sharp boundary identified between the cell wall and the crystal, indicating minimum chemical interaction between the polymer substrate and the crystal

evidence_result.content: Porous foam lowers TENG output relative to dense film.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Compared with the dense film, the porous foam exhibits reduced output performance. The open-circuit voltage decreases from 225.6 ± 0.9 V to 124.5 ± 0.4 V, the short-circuit current density declines from 1.44 ± 0.11 μA cm⁻² to 0.58 ± 0.11 μA cm⁻², and the charge transfer density reduces from 3.46 ± 0.03 nC cm⁻² to 1.83 ± 0.03 nC cm⁻².

evidence_result.content: HKUST-1 partially restores voltage, current density, and charge density.
evidence_result.evidence_span: after incorporation of HKUST-1 fillers, the open-circuit voltage, current density, and charge density recover to 152.3 ± 0.3 V, 0.98 ± 0.11 μA cm⁻², and 2.27 ± 0.03 nC cm⁻², respectively

evidence_result.content: Output remains relatively stable across operating frequencies.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The frequency-dependent output in Figure 3e shows that the output is relatively stable under different operating frequencies.

evidence_result.content: Foam-based TENG reaches maximum power density at 10 MΩ.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The foam-based TENG achieves a maximum power density of 529 mW m⁻² at an optimal external resistance of 10 MΩ.

evidence_result.content: Stiffening occurs when indentation depth reaches the pore diameter, indicating pore collapse.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Stiffening usually takes place when the indentation depth reaches the pore diameter, which clearly suggests pore collapse events.

evidence_result.content: Hysteresis confirms viscoelastic behavior of the porous structure.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The presence of hysteresis between loading and unloading curves further confirms the viscoelastic nature of the porous structure

evidence_result.content: HKUST-1 loading makes the load-depth response more linear with less high-depth stiffening.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Upon incorporation of HKUST-1 fillers, the load-depth response becomes more linear and exhibits reduced stiffening at higher indentation depths.

evidence_result.content: Lower plastic work in HKUST@PA indicates more elastic recovery and less dissipation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the plastic work of the HKUST@PA sample was determined to be 69 ± 3 nJ, compared to 78 ± 3 nJ for the porous PA sample, which indicates a more elastic recovery and less energy dissipation during the unloading step

evidence_result.content: HKUST-1 reinforced porous TENG lacks the abrupt voltage rise seen in unfilled porous samples up to 300 kPa.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the HKUST-1 reinforced porous TENG displays a response similar to the dense sample, with no abrupt increase in voltage observed up to 300 kPa

evidence_result.content: Above strain about 0.13, contact length increases abruptly, marking onset of pore collapse.
evidence_result.evidence_span: beyond a strain of approximately 0.13, an abrupt increase in contact length is observed, indicating the onset of pore collapse

evidence_result.content: Electrical simulation shows higher potential at the same displacement after pore closure.
evidence_result.evidence_span: a significantly higher potential is observed at the same displacement after pore closure

evidence_result.content: Simulations agree well with experiments.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the simulation results are in good correlation with the experimental data

evidence_result.content: Porous structure increases water contact angle relative to dense film.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Compared to dense film, the averaged water contact angle of the porous film increased from ~90° to ~115°, which means the porous structure renders the film more hydrophobic.

evidence_result.content: HKUST-1-loaded porous membrane becomes even more hydrophobic.
evidence_result.evidence_span: infiltration with HKUST-1 renders the porous membrane to become effectively more hydrophobic, with the water contact angle further rising to 119.7°.

evidence_result.content: At low RH, dense and porous films stay stable while HKUST-1-loaded film shows a slight voltage increase.
evidence_result.evidence_span: At low relative humidity levels up to 20%, both the dense and porous films exhibit stable output. In contrast, the HKUST-1 loaded porous membrane shows a slight increase in open circuit voltage from 215 V to 230 V.

evidence_result.content: At higher RH, dense and pristine porous samples lose output rapidly, but HKUST-1-loaded sample declines more slowly and still outputs 21 V at 80% RH.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As the RH increases beyond 30%, the voltage output of the dense and pristine porous samples drops rapidly, approaching nearly zero at elevated humidity levels. In comparison, the HKUST-1-loaded sample shows a milder decline rate and retains a measurable output of 21 V at 80% RH, indicating improved tolerance to moisture.

evidence_result.content: Charge transfer density follows the same trend: initial enhancement then gradual decline with humidity.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The charge transfer density at different humidity levels suggests the same trend. An initial enhancement in output is followed by a gradual decline as the humidity increases.

problem_motivation.content: Porous triboelectric materials/TENGs are promising for performance enhancement, but practical deployment is hindered by structural/performance instability under realistic conditions—especially humidity exposure and repeated high-cycle mechanical loading—creating a need for material designs that preserve long-term mechanical integrity and environmental robustness.
evidence_spans: Porous triboelectric materials offer significant potential for enhancing the performance of triboelectric nanogenerators, yet their practical application is limited by structural instability and humidity-induced performance degradation.

These limitations underscore the need for material design strategies that will simultaneously ensure a long-term mechanical integrity and environmental robustness.

hypothesis_statement.content: The work proposes an integrated composite design strategy for triboelectric systems that combines self-foamed porous/sustainable nylon-like polymer matrices with functional filler reinforcement—specifically HKUST-1—to produce mechanically robust, compliant, and environmentally stable TENGs with improved humidity tolerance, addressing the trade-off between compliance and environmental stability.
evidence_spans: This work demonstrates a strategy that integrates self-foamed porous structures, sustainable polymer design, and functional filler reinforcement to engineer mechanically robust and environmentally stable triboelectric systems.
